angle: Explainable AI for network intrusion detection and network anomaly detection (sibling literature to XAI for traffic classification; shared flow-feature spaces and datasets)

papers.title: AI/ML for Network Security: The Emperor has no Clothes (TRUSTEE)
papers.authors: Arthur Selle Jacobs, Roman Beltiukov, Walter Willinger, Ronaldo A. Ferreira, Arpit Gupta, Lisandro Z. Granville
papers.relevance: TRUSTEE extracts a high-fidelity, size-bounded decision tree plus 'trust report' from any black-box network-security model and uses it to expose underspecification -- shortcut learning, spurious correlations, and out-of-distribution fragility -- in published NIDS/traffic models (incl. Kitsune), making it the central global-explanation hub for this literature.

papers.title: DeepAID: Interpreting and Improving Deep Learning-based Anomaly Detection in Security Applications
papers.authors: Dongqi Han, Zhiliang Wang, Wenqi Chen, Ying Zhong, Su Wang, Han Zhang, Jiahai Yang, Xingang Shi, Xia Yin
papers.relevance: Optimization-based interpretation designed specifically for UNSUPERVISED deep anomaly detectors (evaluated on network detectors incl. Kitsune) with security-tailored constraints (fidelity, conciseness, stability); authors motivate it by noting existing XAI 'are unadaptable for unsupervised DL models'.

papers.title: xNIDS: Explaining Deep Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems for Active Intrusion Responses
papers.authors: Feng Wei, Hongda Li, Ziming Zhao, Hongxin Hu
papers.relevance: Explains DL-NIDS by approximating around history inputs and capturing feature dependencies of structured flow data, then compiles explanations into actionable defense rules; explicitly frames the 'semantic gap between detection results and actionable interpretations' and evaluates on fidelity, sparsity, completeness, stability.

papers.title: CADE: Detecting and Explaining Concept Drift Samples for Security Applications
papers.authors: Limin Yang, Wenbo Guo, Qingying Hao, Arridhana Ciptadi, Ali Ahmadzadeh, Xinyu Xing, Gang Wang
papers.relevance: Contrastive-learning distance space to detect drifting samples plus a distance-based explanation method (explaining 'distance' instead of the decision boundary); case studies include network intrusion detection, directly relevant to drift/OOD explanation in traffic models.

papers.title: An Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Intrusion Detection Systems
papers.authors: Maonan Wang, Kangfeng Zheng, Yanqing Yang, Xiujuan Wang
papers.relevance: The most-cited applied paper of the sub-field: SHAP local+global explanations over IDS models on NSL-KDD, establishing the now-standard 'train detector, run SHAP, plot feature importances' template that hundreds of later papers copy.

papers.title: Evaluating Explanation Methods for Deep Learning in Security
papers.authors: Alexander Warnecke, Daniel Arp, Christian Wressnegger, Konrad Rieck
papers.relevance: Defines the evaluation criteria (descriptive accuracy, sparsity, completeness, stability, efficiency, robustness) for comparing six explanation methods on security DNNs, finding 'significant differences between the methods'; the methodological yardstick reused by NIDS-XAI evaluations.

papers.title: LEMNA: Explaining Deep Learning based Security Applications
papers.authors: Wenbo Guo, Dongliang Mu, Jun Xu, Purui Su, Gang Wang, Xinyu Xing
papers.relevance: Fused-lasso mixture-regression surrogate explanations tailored to RNN/security models with feature dependency; the standard security-specific local-explanation baseline that xNIDS/DeepAID and most NIDS explainers compare against.

papers.title: Explaining Network Intrusion Detection System Using Explainable AI Framework
papers.authors: Shraddha Mane, Dattaraj Rao
papers.relevance: Applies SHAP, LIME, Contrastive Explanations Method, ProtoDash and Boolean Decision Rules to a DNN on NSL-KDD -- one of the widest method-comparison sweeps on a single NIDS model.

papers.title: An Adversarial Approach for Explainable AI in Intrusion Detection Systems
papers.authors: Daniel L. Marino, Chathurika S. Wickramasinghe, Milos Manic
papers.relevance: Early counterfactual-style explanation: finds minimum modifications required to correctly classify misclassified NSL-KDD samples, explaining detector errors -- precursor of the counterfactual NIDS thread.

papers.title: Utilizing XAI technique to improve autoencoder based model for computer network anomaly detection with Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP)
papers.authors: Khushnaseeb Roshan, Aasim Zafar
papers.venue: International Journal of Computer Networks & Communications (IJCNC)
papers.relevance: KernelSHAP on an autoencoder anomaly detector over CICIDS2017 (94% acc, AUC 0.969), using explanations for feature selection to improve the detector -- XAI as a model-improvement loop, not just post-hoc reporting; motivated by the 'black-box nature' obstacle.

papers.title: Using Kernel SHAP XAI Method to Optimize the Network Anomaly Detection Model
papers.authors: Khushnaseeb Roshan, Aasim Zafar
papers.relevance: Follow-up applying KernelSHAP-driven feature optimization to an unsupervised anomaly model on CICIDS2017 (0.90 acc), explicitly noting the difficulty from the 'lack of supervisory nature' of anomalies.

papers.title: An Explainable AI-based Intrusion Detection System for DNS over HTTPS (DoH) Attacks
papers.authors: Tahmina Zebin, Shahadate Rezvy, Yuan Luo
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
papers.relevance: Balanced stacked Random Forest with SHAP feature-contribution analysis on CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 (99.9% P/R/F1) -- a top-venue example of SHAP-explained detection over encrypted-DNS traffic, directly bridging to encrypted traffic classification.

papers.title: "Why Should I Trust Your IDS?": An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Intrusion Detection Systems in Internet of Things Networks
papers.authors: Zakaria Abou El Houda, Bouziane Brik, Lyes Khoukhi
papers.venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
papers.relevance: DNN-based IoT IDS interpreted with RuleFit, LIME and SHAP on NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15; motivated by DL decisions being 'hardly interpreted by users' -- a heavily cited template for multi-method post-hoc explanation.

papers.title: Explainable artificial intelligence for intrusion detection in IoT networks: A deep learning based approach
papers.authors: Bhawana Sharma, Lokesh Sharma, Chhagan Lal, Satyabrata Roy
papers.relevance: DNN IoT-IDS explained with RuleFit, LIME and SHAP (local and global) on NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15 -- among the most-cited journal instances of the standard SHAP/LIME-on-IDS recipe.

papers.title: Classification and Explanation for Intrusion Detection System Based on Ensemble Trees and SHAP Method
papers.authors: Thi-Thu-Huong Le, Haeyoung Kim, Hyoeun Kang, Howon Kim
papers.relevance: Decision-tree/Random-Forest ensembles explained with TreeSHAP on NetFlow-based NF-BoT-IoT-v2, NF-ToN-IoT-v2 and IoTDS20 -- notable for using the standardized NetFlow feature sets shared with traffic-classification work.

papers.title: Toward Enhanced Attack Detection and Explanation in Intrusion Detection System-Based IoT Environment Data
papers.authors: Thi-Thu-Huong Le et al.
papers.relevance: Extends the ensemble+SHAP line toward attack explanation on IoT IDS data, surfaced by the counterfactual/explanation query on OpenAlex (76 citations).

papers.title: Robust Network Intrusion Detection Through Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI)

papers.relevance: Two-stage pipeline: XGBoost detector explained with SHAP, whose explanations feed an autoencoder that flags novel/unseen attacks on NSL-KDD -- explanations used operationally for OOD detection rather than only for transparency.

papers.title: Explainable AI for Intrusion Detection Systems: LIME and SHAP Applicability on Multi-Layer Perceptron

papers.relevance: Systematic study of LIME/SHAP applicability and perturbation behavior on MLP-based IoT intrusion detection, aimed at making explanations usable by cybersecurity experts.

papers.title: Evaluating Standard Feature Sets Towards Increased Generalisability and Explainability of ML-Based Network Intrusion Detection

notes: RECURRING DATASETS (frequency order): NSL-KDD (still the default despite its age), CICIDS2017 / CSE-CIC-IDS2018, UNSW-NB15, the NetFlow-standardized NF-v2 family (NF-UNSW-NB15-v2, NF-BoT-IoT-v2, NF-ToN-IoT-v2 -- Sarhan/Layeghy/Portmann line, shared with traffic-classification work), ToN-IoT, Edge-IIoTset, KDD99 (LLM papers), CTU-13, InSDN, CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 (DoH), RoEduNet-SIMARGL2021, Kitsune/Mirai captures, VeReMi (VANET) and HCRL Car-Hacking (CAN). RECURRING EXPLANATION METHODS: SHAP overwhelmingly dominant (TreeSHAP for ensembles, KernelSHAP for autoencoders/unsupervised, DeepSHAP for DNNs); LIME second; then RuleFit, Integrated Gradients, DeepLIFT, LRP, occlusion sensitivity, attention visualization, decision-tree/rule extraction as global surrogates (TRUSTEE, eclectic rule extraction, autoencoder rule extraction, ExAI5G's IG+surrogate tree), counterfactuals (adversarial minimal-modification Marino 2018; tabular diffusion Galwaduge 2025; graph counterfactuals ProvX), prototypes (ProtoDash), distance-based explanation of drift (CADE), optimization-based interpretation for unsupervised models (DeepAID), mixture-regression surrogate (LEMNA), SOM visual explanations (Ables), and LLM-generated natural-language narratives (HuntGPT, eX-NIDS, EXP-SEC). RECURRING MODELS BEING EXPLAINED: XGBoost/RF/ensemble trees, MLP/DNN, CNN and CNN-LSTM hybrids, autoencoders and VAEs (Kitsune, LENS-XAI), GNNs (E-GraphSAGE/Anomal-E), transformers/TabNet, and federated variants of all of these (a 2025-2026 boom: FL+SHAP appears in dozens of venues). AUTHOR-STATED LIMITATIONS / FUTURE WORK (the gold for a related-work gap paragraph): (1) Explanation disagreement -- Subasi et al.: 'inconsistent influential features across different explanation methods'; Kumar & Thing: 'XAI explanations generated using different tools are in conflict'; E-XAI 'shows the limitations and strengths of current XAI when applied to network IDS'. (2) No human evaluation -- Nadeem SoK: 'user studies for explanation evaluation are conducted in only 14% of the cases' and XAI apps are 'designed with little understanding of how they might be integrated into analyst workflows'; HuntGPT motivated by dashboards having 'seen limited acceptance from incident responders'; (EC)2 (arXiv 2607.26201): 'feature-level explanations for anomaly detectors offer limited value' to analysts. (3) Missing explainability metrics -- Neupane X-IDS survey explicitly calls for defining explainability metrics for IDS; Warnecke et al. supply the only widely reused criteria (fidelity/sparsity/stability/efficiency/robustness); xNIDS adds completeness for actionable response. (4) Unsupervised gap -- DeepAID: existing interpretation approaches 'are unadaptable for unsupervised DL models'; Roshan & Zafar: difficulty from the 'lack of supervisory nature' of anomalies. (5) Shortcut learning / underspecification -- TRUSTEE finds shortcut learning, spurious correlations and OOD vulnerability in published models; Corea et al.: 'most classifiers leverage only less than three critical features'; Layeghy's cross-domain work shows attributions differ across domains (models don't transfer). (6) Interpretability-accuracy trade-off -- Ables et al. quantify white-box SOMs at '1%-3% less than' black-box accuracy. (7) Adversarial/robustness caveats -- Singh et al.: 'real-time deployment and performance under adversarial conditions require further investigation'; Khan et al. survey 'Adversarial XIDS' (attacking the explanations); Yasarathna SoK wants 'explainable AI-driven security frameworks' as future work. (8) Computational cost -- KernelSHAP repeatedly flagged as too slow for line-rate traffic; motivates lightweight/distilled designs (LENS-XAI, RIDE memristor trees, TinyML XIDS). (9) LLMs -- Houssel et al.: 'LLMs are unfit for detection' but promising 'as complementary agents' for explanation. METHODOLOGICAL NOTE ON SOURCES: Semantic Scholar API returned HTTP 429 (shared anonymous pool exhausted) for every attempt (both via WebFetch and local PowerShell), so citation counts are from OpenAlex where retrieved and set to 0 where unknown; corpus was assembled from arXiv API, OpenAlex, DBLP (local fetch) and WebSearch, with every listed paper coming from an actually-retrieved result. DBLP's 2025-2026 slice shows the field's long tail: dozens of near-identical 'ensemble/DL + SHAP/LIME on IoT benchmark' journal papers -- useful as evidence of method monoculture when writing the gap analysis.
